title: Poem - No Further Action Needed Now
html:
In the corners of our minds, where shadows often tread,
The autopilot of our lives, a constant hum, a thread.
Noticing each subtle shift, a whisper, a glance, a sigh,
Readying for imagined threats, as moments drift by.

In this ceaseless vigilance, our energies deplete,
For every hint of danger met, our peace we slowly cheat.
What if in the calm of breath, we chose a different way,
To tune into the feeling-tone, and softly, gently say:

“No action needed now, let stillness be our guide,
Release the stress, the weary heart, and let it subside.”
We reclaim the balance life bestows,
And in the peace, our spirit gently grows.

For in the space of simple breath, a revolution lies,
To let go of the needless strife, and see with clearer eyes.
In each deliberate choice to rest, our strength is truly found,
The quiet power of a soul, in harmony unbound.

So let us walk this mindful path, with my gentle might,
To find our calm amidst the storm, to turn towards the light.
For in each “no action needed,” a tranquil heart can see,
The way to live with open joy, authentically free.

title: Poem - The Quiet Light Within
html:
There is a quiet light that lives inside you,
a steady flame unseen by hurried eyes,
yet it burns with a truth
no storm can extinguish.

In the mirror of morning, you glimpse it—
a spark of something more,
more than the self you’ve known,
more than the name you wear like a well-worn coat,
something wild, something tender, something utterly your own.

In the hush of evening, it waits for you,
a whisper in the wind, a gentle nudge from within,
saying, Here you are.
Here you’ve always been.

This light is not for others to see,
though it colours the world with every step you take.
It is the song you have always sung,
in the silence of your heart, in the quiet of your dreams.

There is a strength in you that bends, but does not break,
a resilience born from a thousand dawns,
from the simple act of being yourself,
again, and again.

So stand, not as a mountain,
but as a river— flowing, shaping,
finding your way through the rocks and the trees,
and in every curve, celebrating the journey that is yours alone.

For in this quiet light, you are whole, you are enough,
and the world is brighter for the gift of your presence,
for the gift of your unique,
unrepeatable soul.

title: Poem - The Circle of Peace
html:
In the quiet of the morning, where the light meets the day,
Let your mind rest gently, let your worries drift away.
For within your tender heart, lies a circle, deep and wide,
Where the storms of thought may gather, but peace shall abide.

When the mind stirs the body, in a dance of fear and pain,
Remember, dear soul, this cycle need not reign.
The thoughts may come like shadows, darkening your view,
But know they hold no power, unless you say they do.

For the body is a mirror, reflecting what the mind creates,
It trembles with the echoes of the mind’s imagined fates.
Yet, in each breath, a chance to break the spell,
To calm the rising tide, where peace and stillness dwell.

Breathe in the light of dawn, breathe out the shades of night,
Release the fears that bind you, let your spirit take flight.
In the space between each thought, lies a world of pure grace,
Where the body and the mind find their sacred place.

Do not fight the thoughts, let them come and let them go,
Like leaves upon the river, drifting in the flow.
For in letting go, you find the truth within,
The circle of peace begins, where fear does end.

So, sit with me in silence, and feel the breath of life,
Let go of all the worries, all the inner strife.
For in the quiet stillness, where the heart beats true,
You’ll find the circle of peace, and it shall renew you.

title: Poem - A Soft Embrace of Shadows
html:
There is a place, where low mood rests,
a silent corner of the heart, where shadows gather,
not to overwhelm, but to remind you,
of the delicate dance, between light and dark.

Here, in the quiet, you sit,
not as a conqueror,
but as a witness,
to the ebb and flow, of all that is human.

You do not need to love the grey, that brushes the edges of your day,
nor the heaviness, that drapes itself, like an uninvited guest.
But you can acknowledge it,
with the softest whisper, “This too, is part of me.”

In this tender recognition, the heart, once clenched, begins to unfold,
petal by petal, towards the light,
towards the memory, of a sunlit path,
a forest drenched in gold.

And so you choose, not to banish the shadows,
but to hold them, with the gentlest of hands,
and then, with a breath, you turn your gaze,
to the warmth, to the places, where joy still lingers.

For you are both, the darkness and the light, the sorrow and the song,
and in this knowing, lies the quiet courage,
to carry on, to live fully,
in the soft embrace, of all that you are.

title: Poem - The Space Between Us
html:
In the quiet of the morning,
before the world takes its first breath,
there is a space between us —
a place where words are not spoken,
but felt, like the earth feels the weight of the sun’s first light.

You turn to me, not with questions,
but with the silent need for belief,
for something that only grows
when tended by hands that understand the fragility of touch.

I have learned that to love you is to learn the rhythm of your heart,
to speak less of what I need and more of what you already carry
the unspoken burden of a man
who builds his world from the ground up.

Here, in this space, I give you the respect that lifts your chest in the morning
and softens your shoulders at night.
I offer you not judgment, but patience, not correction, but admiration,
for it is in the seeing of your efforts,
not the overlooking of your flaws, that we come to know each other.

You are not a question to be answered, but a presence to be honoured,
and in the quiet spaces of our day, I remind you of this—not in loud declarations,
but in the softness of my hand on yours,
the light in my eyes when you speak of your dreams.

For I have learned that love does not demand, it creates room for growth.
And if I wish to see you rise, then I must rise beside you,
offering you the quiet strength that whispers, “I see you,”
in a world too quick to turn away.

This is the way we walk together not as shadows chasing light,
but as two bodies moving toward it,
with tenderness enough to fill the gaps
between our separate steps.

And if you falter, know this:
I will not pull you back, nor push you forward,
but stand with you in the stillness,
until you are ready to find the way again.

For love, true love, is not a destination,
but the way we walk alongside each other.

title: Poem - No Further Action Needed
html:
Here we stand, in the quiet curve of dawn,
where the city breathes and the heart rests.
No rush, no call, no demand –
just the stillness that says, You are enough.

Let the morning rise around us,
soft like the brush of a whispered thought.
In the space between, we find what was always waiting –
not a task, but a tenderness, an opening to who we truly are.

Together, in this simple moment,
we touch the edge of being.
No need to reach for more, no need to fix or fight.
The heart knows its way home, if we listen.

This is where love resides –
not in action, but in presence.
Not in striving, but in the gentle release
of everything that says, Do more.

We are here, now, in the fullness of our quiet selves.
And in this togetherness, we discover,
there is no further action needed—
just the grace of being, in the stillness of our shared breath.

Let us stay awhile,
and let that be enough.

title: Poem - For what it is Worth
html:
In the heart of concrete canyons,
Where the city’s breath hums cold and grey,
A quiet figure sits, eyes closed,
Amongst the rush, the noise, the sway.

But here, in the stillness,
There is a bloom unseen, a light unfelt—
A moment where the world softens,
And all the striving begins to melt.

The walls, though hard, hold space for you,
Each crack, a story of how you’ve grown.
This stillness, it is yours to claim,
A place where you are never alone.

Feel the warmth within, the gentle rise,
Of breath, of pulse, of heart in beat.
You are more than the rush outside,
You are the love that makes you complete.

So, rest in this knowing, hold it close,
In silence, your worth begins to show.
For here, in the urban jungle’s heart,
You are the calm, the root that grows.

title: Poem - A Gentle Pause
html:
In the rush of the day, where time slips away,
And the world spins fast, with no time to stay,
There’s a whisper, soft, from deep within,
A voice that says, “It’s time to begin.”

Not with the tasks, or the endless grind,
But with the heart, and a softer mind.
A breath, a pause, a moment to feel,
The quiet call that’s ever so real.

For in caring for others, you often forget,
The one who needs kindness hasn’t been met.
So stop for a while, let the world turn slow,
Breathe deep, and let your spirit grow.

A sip of stillness, a touch of grace,
To heal the parts you’ve left in haste.
Your needs are worthy, your soul is bright,
In tending to you, you reclaim your light.

So in the busy, find that space,
A loving hand, a gentle embrace.
And remember, dear one, it’s always true,
The world can wait while you care for you.

title: Poem - In the Garden of Worth
html:
In the quiet heart of the world,
where soft whispers rise like dawn,
there blooms a place, gentle and warm,
where we belong, just as we are.

In this garden of self and soul,
every petal is a part of you—
rooted deep, growing tall,
worthy of light, of love, of truth.

Smile and know your worth,
like earth that holds each tender seed,
for you are here to bloom, to breathe,
to trust the love that you receive.

Be kind to the soft places,
where doubt and worry dwell.
For even shadows long to know
the warmth of care, the peace of self.

Let the world feel your kindness,
let it rest within your hands,
for as you love, the garden grows,
and we are all flowers in this land.

You are enough, in every way,
and in each quiet breath you take,
there’s space for joy, for peace, for grace—
for you are loved, without mistake.

So breathe deep, and gently smile,
you’re worthy, whole, and strong,
held by the world, by self, by all,
in this sanctuary where you belong.

title: Poem - A Light Within
html:
In times when shadows cross our way,
And words feel too small to hold the day,
Know that within, a light is there,
A glow of strength, beyond compare.

Though paths may wind and seem unsure,
Your heart holds courage, strong and pure.
With each small step, no matter how,
You’re braver than you feel right now.

Lean on the love that’s all around,
In whispered words, in steady ground.
This journey’s yours, but not alone—
We’re here beside you, stone by stone.

So take your time, and breathe in deep,
Allow yourself the space to keep
The hope alive, the faith to see
That healing comes, as wild and free.

And even when the road seems long,
Remember this—your spirit’s strong.
You’re not defined by what you face;
You’re endless strength, boundless grace.

title: Poem - The Warmth Within
html:
Awake, the world still wrapped in night,
A tender glow begins its flight.
Not from the sun, not from the fire,
But from the heart’s most true desire.

A quiet breath, a gentle pause,
No need for judgment, rules, or laws.
In stillness grows a steady flame,
A whisper soft: You are the same.

The same as stars, the earth, the sea,
Worthy, whole—just meant to be.
No need to strive, no need to prove,
Just let the warmth within you move.

It spreads, it soothes, it softly mends,
Through cracks and corners, twists and bends.
A practice simple, yet profound,
Where love for self is freely found.

So light your fire, let it stay,
To warm your heart throughout the day.
In knowing worth, we truly start—
To hold the world with an open heart.

title: Poem - A Gentle Whisper to Your Heart
html:
My dear, rest now, for you’ve carried much,
The weight of worlds held in your tender touch.
But even the strongest must pause and mend,
To love yourself is where you begin, not end.

You are not the flaws you see or fear,
You are the light that draws others near.
In your chest beats a heart so divine,
Worthy of love, just as it shines.

Forgive the stumble, the hurried pace,
Let grace and kindness fill that space.
For in each breath, a soft rebirth,
A reminder: you are endless worth.

So cradle yourself as the night holds the stars,
With hands that heal, no matter the scars.
Smile inward, and softly say,
“I am enough, in every way.”

title: Poem - A Whisper to Myself
html:
Oh child of my heart, so tender, so true,
Do you see the light that shines within you?
Each step you take, though burdened or free,
Carries a beauty only love can see.

Your hands, though weary, have given so much,
Your soul, so gentle, heals with its touch.
When shadows fall and doubt takes its place,
Know you are wrapped in infinite grace.

Be kind to yourself, as the morning to the dew,
For the world is brighter because it holds you.
Beloved, remember, in all that you do—
You are enough, simply for being you.

title: Poem - Start Within
html:
In the quiet chambers of your heart,
where whispers of doubt and longing start,
there lies a flame, tender and small,
a warmth that waits to answer your call.

Do not seek outside for what’s already near,
the comfort, the strength to banish the fear.
Begin with yourself, this sacred ground,
where the seeds of belonging are first found.

With gentle breath, tend this fire,
no need for perfection, no need to aspire.
In your own embrace, you’ll find a peace,
a quiet love that grants release.

For when you hold yourself so dear,
the world feels closer, love draws near.
And what you give, so freely bestowed,
comes from a well that’s always flowed.

So start within, let kindness grow,
a light to guide through the coldest snow.
In this connection, you’ll surely see,
we are one, bound in humanity.

title: Poem - A Gentle Return to You
html:
When the storm has passed, and the silence begins,
Come back to yourself—softly, kindly, as a friend.
Breathe deep, dear heart, let the weight fall away,
You are not the words they spoke, nor the games they play.

Let your shoulders drop, release the tight hold,
You are not their fire, their anger, their cold.
You are the calm beneath the crashing waves,
The stillness in the forest, the peace that saves.

Rest in your breath; it will carry you home,
To the quietest parts where you’re never alone.
Here, the world cannot bruise or pull you apart,
You are whole, you are loved, in the depths of your heart.

Wrap yourself in kindness, in words soft and true,
“I am worthy of care. I am enough, just as I am, too.”
Nurture yourself as the earth tends a flower—
With patience, with love, in your gentlest hour.

Let the encounter fall like leaves to the ground,
What matters now is the peace you’ve found.
Here, in the warmth of your heart’s embrace,
You are home, you are safe, in your own sacred space.

title: Poem - A Gentle Beginning
html:
Sit softly in the morning light,
where the world is still,
and the breath whispers its quiet song.
Here, in the tender pause,
you find the courage to begin.

The first step is not a leap,
nor a bold shout into the wind.
It is the smallest movement of your heart,
a whisper of yes,
a promise to meet the day with care.

Feel the ground beneath you,
steady, unbroken.
Feel the breath within you,
a quiet rhythm that carries hope.
This is your anchor, your guide—
the place where action takes root.

The world does not ask for greatness,
only presence.
A willingness to rise,
to see the possibility in each moment,
and to step forward with love and intention.

In this stillness,
you hold the power to change the day,
to take the first step,
and with it,
shape the path that unfolds ahead.

title: Poem - The Quiet Flame
html:
Hope is not a roaring fire,
not the bold strike of a match,
nor the sudden burst of light.
It is the quiet flame that lingers long after the spark.

It does not demand perfection,
nor does it ask for certainty.
It simply whispers, Begin again,
and finds strength in the attempt.

There is no shame in the falling — only in forgetting
the resilience that lifts you once more.
Each rise, each step,
a testament to the depth of your spirit.

In the stillness of this moment,
feel the breath that carries you,
the pulse of life steady beneath your skin.
This is your anchor, your compass,
the proof that you are already enough.

When the waves of doubt roll in,
remember the vast ocean beneath,
unmoved by the surface storm.
Here lies your strength— not in unbroken paths,
but in the courage to walk them,
one step, one breath, one flame at a time.

Hope is yours to hold,
not as a fleeting wish,
but as a promise to yourself:
I will stay, I will rise,
I will walk through this life with open arms.

title: Poem - A Gentle Space for Fear
html:
Come, sit beside me.
Lay down the weight you carry,
not to rid yourself of it,
but to rest your hands
from holding so tightly.

Fear is not your enemy,
nor your master,
nor a thing to banish.
It is a whisper at the door,
a quiet voice asking,
May I be seen?

Let it be seen.
Not with judgment,
not with scorn,
but with the softest gaze
you can offer.

Hold it as you would
a trembling bird,
fragile but alive,
uncertain, yet full of flight.

Ask it, What do you need?
Ask it, What are you here to teach me?
And in that asking,
watch the tight fist loosen,
watch the weight become breath,
watch the walls around your heart
melt into open sky.

Fear is just a visitor.
You are the home.

title: Poem - A Gentle Space for Fear II
html:
Come, sit with me.
Lay down the weight you carry,
not to cast it away,
but to rest your hands from holding so tightly.

Fear is not your enemy,
nor your master, nor a thing to banish.
It is a whisper in the wind,
a ripple in the water, a visitor, asking to be seen.

Let it be seen.
Not with resistance, not with scorn,
but with the softest gaze you can offer.

Breathe.
Feel the air move through you,
like waves on the shore,
like the hush of morning light.

There is no rush.
No need to force, no need to fix.
Let fear sit beside you, small and quiet,
while you open the sky within.

Hold this moment as it is.
Let it be vast, let it be kind.
You are not the storm,
but the sky that holds it.

title: Poem - The Doorway of Fear
html:
Come, sit beside me.
Not to fight, not to flee,
but to listen—to the quiet space
between the inhale and the exhale,
where fear softens into breath.

Fear is not a wall,
though it may seem solid.
It is a doorway, closed but waiting,
its handle cool beneath your hand,
its hinges willing to turn.

Ask, not with trembling,
but with wonder:
What lies beyond?
What if this is not an ending,
but a beginning in disguise?

Let the question be enough.
Let the air between you
and the unknown
be spacious, light.

You do not have to step through today.
Only stand at the threshold,
breathing,
curious.

title: Poem - A Step Forward
html:
Come, stand with me.
Not in stillness, not in waiting,
but in the quiet hum of readiness,
where breath meets intention,
where the earth rises to meet your step.

Fear does not own this path,
though it lingers at the edges,
whispering its familiar tune.
Let it sing—
but do not let it steer.

What is the smallest step?
Not the perfect one,
not the grandest—
just the next,
the one that carries you forward
without demand, without force,
but with a gentle unfolding.

Feel the ground beneath you.
It is steady,
it is patient,
it does not ask you to leap—
only to move,
to shift,
to begin.

One step,
then another.
That is all it takes
for the path to reveal itself.

title: Poem - A Grounding in Uncertainty
html:
When the winds of change are howling near,
And doubt is whispering in your ear,
Pause… and listen, soft and slow,
There is more within you than you know.

A breath, a touch, a steady ground,
A moment where the heart is found.
Not in the past, nor racing ahead,
But here, where trust and hope are bred.

The sky still holds the morning light,
The stars still shine through deepest night.
And though the path may twist and weave,
You are held in all you grieve.

No need for answers, clear and bright,
Just one small step into the light.
For even in the unknown’s embrace,
Love and wisdom find their place.

So breathe, dear soul, and softly be,
There is space for you in all you see.
With every whisper, every sigh,
The earth still turns, the sun will rise.

title: Poem - Becoming Soft
html:
Be soft, where once you were stone.
Let the winds of change shape you,
Not as a thing to be broken,
But as something willing to bend.

Be kind, where once you held fear.
See the world not as battle,
Not as weight to be carried,
But as a river to step into,
Cool and welcoming, ready to hold you.

Be open, where once you were closed.
Let your thoughts be leaves,
Drifting, floating, never clinging,
Trusting the current to carry them where it will.

Be whole, where once you were divided.
You are not a puzzle to solve,
Not a story with missing pages,
But a tide that rises, falls, and rises again.

Be here, where once you were lost.
Not chasing, not resisting,
But standing, breathing, knowing—
This moment is enough.
And so are you.

title: Poem - Softening into now
html:
Here, in this quiet place,
the breath whispers gently through my bones,
like wind that loosens the leaves,
like light touching the edge of every anxious thought.

My mind, once clenched as tightly as a fist,
slowly unfolds into openness,
into softness,
with each breath.

The subtle easing of my jaw,
the gentle lowering of my shoulders—
these tiny gestures are quiet invitations to meet myself again,
to greet the day softly without armour.

Here, now, I discover that I am more spacious
than the stories I tell myself,
wider than worry,
more gentle than the shadows of fear passing through.

In this quiet unfolding,
I sense how the river inside flows freely,
when the banks are no longer tight.

Together, we sit in stillness,
knowing the softness of mind is the courage of heart—
the courage to remain open,
to welcome all things with kindness.

Let this softness linger,
let it guide me through the day,
reminding me who I truly am—
a gentle observer, awake, alive,
at ease with this breath, this moment, this life.

title: Poem - Hands Unfolding
html:
There is a secret language the body speaks softly—
words in silent gestures,
whispered in the opening of fingers,
the gentle unfolding of palms.

Notice how tightly fists hold stories,
years of quiet resistance,
yet see how easily the hands drop their weight,
spreading open,
like petals meeting sunlight for the first time.

Each subtle release a choice to soften,
to let go of struggle,
to welcome the world again,
to remember your place—

A gentle part of everything,
connecting and reconnecting,
softening, healing, and rediscovering your nature,
one subtle movement at a time.

Hold your own softness gently,
carry this openness forward,
and find, again and again,
the quiet strength of being fully here,
is in every moment

title: Poem - Listening to the Stillness
html:
There is a hush between the breath,
a place where the world waits,
not for you to move,
not for you to do,
but for you to listen.

The rising and the falling,
the way the air enters,
not as a visitor,
but as something that has always known the shape of your ribs,
the weight of your longing.

In this stillness,
your life gathers itself,
not in the chase of distant horizons,
not in the reaching for more,
but here—inside the quiet tide,
inside the slow turning
of all you have been
toward all you are becoming.

This breath,
this one,
is the only doorway you need.

title: Poem - A quiet invitation
html:
In this early stillness,
morning’s gentle breath
slips softly beneath
the mind’s noisy threshold—
a silent offering,
asking nothing,
yet opening everything.

Sit down, it says,
with the hidden self,
the deep inner silence
waiting beneath
all urgency.

Here, your breath
is an ancient language
longing to speak again—
here, the dawn
is a conversation
between who you are
and who you might yet become.

Let yourself arrive,
fully and quietly,
in the honest grace
of this simple hour.

title: Poem - The warmth of your soul
html:
Let the warmth in your stomach be the warmth of your soul,
a quiet ember glowing softly within,
a place untouched by the rushing world,
where stillness meets breath,
where ease unfolds.

Let it be the sun behind the clouds,
the gentle radiance that does not demand,
but simply offers—
a quiet presence, a deep knowing,
that you are safe, you are here,
and you belong.

Feel it rise with every breath,
spreading like morning light through the body,
not needing to prove itself,
not needing to hold on—
just warmth, just presence, just you.

Let the tightness dissolve like mist,
let the heart rest against the softness of being.
You are not separate from this warmth.
You are not apart from this light.
You are simply home.

title: Poem - The Way Joy Comes
html:
It does not arrive
like the windstorm,
breaking branches
or shouting through the trees.

It comes
as a small bird
you didn’t see at first—
only the tilt of a leaf gave it away,
and the hush that followed.

Joy waits
until the body forgets its armour,
until the breath becomes a soft river
and the hands—
once fists—open
like petals at dawn.

It does not demand.
It does not explain itself.

But if you smile,
even slightly,
and sit still
as if you were listening for the hooves
of a deer in deep forest,
you may feel it—

a warmth behind the ribs,
a lifting under the chest,
a quiet rising
like sap in spring
that doesn’t need to say
where it’s going.

And you,
having done nothing
but rest in the light,
will remember
you were always meant
to feel this alive.

title: Poem - Where I Begin Again
html:
I searched the forest,
boots deep in the softened earth,
for something called ground—
as if it had been lost
beneath the weight of my thoughts.

The wind passed through me like memory.
The birds went on as if I had never left.

But then—
in the pause between two breaths,
I felt it:
my feet,
still here.
The curve of my spine,
not broken but bowed in silence.

My fingers curled slightly,
not in defence—
in belonging.
The floor did not fall.
The air held.

Somewhere beneath the stories,
beneath the tremble and noise,
was a quiet animal
that had never stopped waiting.

And when I listened—
truly listened—
I found that I was already home.
Not in the world.
But in this small body
willing to feel
again.

title: Poem - The long path
html:
It does not happen all at once—
this becoming.
Like the tree that thickens by quiet rings,
or the stream that carves the stone
with no rush,
only persistence.

You rise each day
not to change the world,
but to meet it.
To greet the wind with your face,
and the soil with your steps.
To say yes again and again
to your own unfolding.

The robin does not apologise
for yesterday’s song.
She sings anew,
because that is what she is made for.

And you—
aren’t you also made
for motion and stillness,
for courage tucked quietly
beneath your ribcage,
for the slow return
to your deepest self?

Some days you will fly.
Others, barely move.
Both are holy.
Both are enough.

Let the forest remind you—
growth isn’t loud.
It’s the moss creeping in,
the fern unfurling,
the self you’re becoming
stepping out,
again and again,
into the light.

title: Poem - Where the mind rests
html:
There is a place the mind can go
when it’s had enough of spinning—
not far, not high,
not away, but down.

Into the quiet bowl of the body
where the ribs rise and fall
like gentle hills
beneath the wind.

There—clarity does not arrive
with trumpets,
but like mist lifting
from a field at first light.

It reveals what was always there:
the path, the stone,
the sound of your own feet
coming home.

You do not chase focus—
you let the breath find it,
curling softly around your spine,
rooting you like pine into earth.

And suddenly,
without force,
the scattered birds of thought still themselves
on the branches of your being.

You remember— you are not lost.
You are listening.
And you have always known
the way.

title: Poem - The One Who Waited
html:
Today, you found her —
the one who never left.
The small, shining one,
tucked beneath your errands and your grief,
patient as rain falling beyond the window.

She did not cry out.
She did not stamp her feet.
She sat quietly, hands folded,
watching the seasons change
inside your hurried mind.

And when you turned —
softened by some ache you could not name —
she smiled,
and it was enough.

No reprimand, no sorrow,
only the clear water of welcome.

Come now, she says,
we have been waiting long enough.
Let us walk home together.

title: Poem - To the worried mind
html:
You’ve been pacing again—
running circles around
what hasn’t happened,
what might,
what already hurt.

I know.
You mean well.
You want to keep me safe.
You tighten the chest,
speed the heart,
whisper what-ifs
like prayers in reverse.

But look—
I’m here.
Not in the future.
Not in the past.

Here, where the ground holds me,
where the breath moves in and out
without asking why.

Here,
in the warmth of hands,
the weight of legs,
the soft rhythm of my own pulse under skin.

You don’t have to do it all.
You don’t have to shout.
I hear you—
but I’m back now.

And I will stay
right here in this body that is mine,
where peace is not the absence of worry—
but the presence of knowing
I’ve come home.

title: Poem - To the one I forgot
html:
You were always here,
weren’t you?
Even when I wandered
through noise and striving,
you stayed behind—
quiet,
soft-spoken,
keeping a place warm
just beneath my ribs.

I looked for answers
in schedules,
in approval,
in the endless lists.
But you waited—
not hurt,
just patient,
as only the body can be.

This morning,
I returned.
No fanfare,
just a breath,
a shift in the spine,
a hand on my chest.

And there you were,
smiling like the first light—
not asking where I’d been,
only glad
I’d finally come home.

title: Poem - The Way Home
html:
You do not have to be perfect.
Only present.
Only willing to feel the weight
of a sparrow’s wing,
the hush of breath before it names itself.

This work—
is not about fixing.
It is the soft tending,
the hush that enters
when a hand meets the chest
and waits.

There is a trail
that runs through the forest of the body,
not marked on any map.
But when walked with kindness,
the trees lean closer,
the stones remember your name.

You have heard it—
that whisper beneath the noise:
come home, come home.
And now you carry it
in the cupped bowl of your voice
for others to hear.

You will not need to shout.
Only to walk slowly,
and breathe,
and remind them
that the door has always been open.

The Way Quiet Finds Me

This morning, I did not chase the sky.
I let it open above me—vast,
blue as a bowl turned by some ancient hand—
and I let it be enough.

No need to spill myself into the day,
no need to sparkle or sing
or scatter words like startled birds.
Instead, I pressed my tongue
to the soft cathedral of my mouth and listened
to the hush inside the forest of my ribs.

A micro-smile found me—
not the broad one that dazzles and dances,
but the kind that curls inward,
like a fern unfolding at dawn.

The earth was still damp with its dreaming.
I touched my thighs with steady palms
and remembered:
this body is a boundary, and also a field—
ripe with the wild wheat of being.

When the wind stirred,
I did not rush to follow.
When the swallows wheeled above the marsh,
I watched without needing to rise.
I swallowed once, softly.
My jaw unclenched its ambitions.

And oh—how calm is a sky
that does not demand performance.
How kind is the breath that only asks to be felt,
not shaped.

So here I sit— with the stillness,
with the trees,
with the hush between heartbeats.
And I say to myself,
You are allowed to rest.
You are allowed to feel joy without flight.

The world does not need your fire every hour.
Sometimes, it only needs your embers.

Stillness at the End

You were never loud about your goodness—
you simply moved through the days
with the steady hands of someone
who had made peace with work,
with silence,
with the weight of things not spoken.

You taught me
how to listen by how you listened,
how to stay by how you stayed—
not clinging, not demanding,
just there.
Like the shape of a harbour
welcomes the tide.

You weren’t a man of ceremony,
but you made the ordinary sacred—
a chair by the window,
the folding of a shirt,
a look that said more than words
would dare to.

And in the end,
there was no thunder,
no last performance.
Just breath that softened into air,
hands that let go without struggle,
and your cheek, still warm
as the morning rose.

If this was goodbye,
then let it be known:
you were
a man who loved well,
and was well loved.

And I—
who once reached up for your hand,
now carry your stillness in mine.

title: Poem - The Smallest Turning
html:
I went out early—
mist still clinging to the alder trees,
dew on the moss like a thousand yeses.
A wren, that holy whisper of the hedgerow,
shivered once and stilled the hush around it.

And I thought—
how little it takes.
A tilt of the beak.
A breath held, then freed.

Inside me, too,
something turned—
not with a clang, but a leaning,
barely a breath’s worth of courage
toward kindness.

Not the grand vow,
but the softened jaw.
Not the roaring change,
but the gentle swallow of being.

And yet—
didn’t the meadow respond?
Didn’t the wind pause,
as if waiting for me to become
just a little more real?

The world is made of such shifts—
quiet as seed sprouting in darkness,
bold as a smile in the face of fear.

So today,
I will honour the tiniest movement—
the lifting of the brow,
the loosening of the chest,
the un-gripping of the hand.

These are the revolutions
the hawk rides on,
the tide listens for,
the stars obey.

title: Poem - The wild inside me
html:
Not all forests
are made of trees.
Some grow quietly
beneath the ribs—
a tangle of memory and longing,
soft light
filtering through the canopy of thought.

This morning,
before the birds,
I wandered inward.
Past the doubt,
past the ache to do more,
into a clearing
of breath and silence.

There,
the wild part of me—
not lost,
just waiting—
looked up and smiled.

It asked for no words.
Only that I stay a while,
and remember
I belong.

title: Poem - Before the day begins
html:
Before the kettle sings,
before the sun rounds the edge
of the garden wall,
I sit.

The world is not asking yet—
not for words,
or effort,
or cleverness.

Only breath.
Only this quiet,
like the hush before birds
decide to speak.

I do not reach for answers.
I let the silence
unfold its soft robe,
and wrap it gently
around the hum
in my chest.

In this stillness,
I remember:
there is nothing to prove.
No race to run.

There is only
the wide sky of now,
the steady tide of breath,
and the way peace
waits patiently—
just beneath
the noise.

title: Poem - Where the Wind Once Carried His Voice
html:
I went to the place where the grasses lean—
where the wind moves like a memory across the land,
and the crows speak in riddles
he would have understood.

The sky was the kind of blue
that doesn’t ask for anything,
and still, I gave it my sorrow,
tucked in the hem of my coat like a letter
never quite posted.

I thought of his hands—
how they built and fixed and held
without ceremony.
The way he looked at trees
as if they might answer something.

Today, I saw one standing alone,
its roots sunk deep in silence,
its branches lifting
the way he once lifted me
onto his shoulders to see further.

The ache in my chest,
sharp as the first frost on the fields,
softened—
not because I missed him less
but because I remembered more.

The quiet moments.
The way he paused before speaking.
How he never needed the spotlight,
only the steadiness of earth beneath him.

I did not know that grief
could be an open gate—
that if I stood still enough,
it would become
a passage to gratitude.

Now, the breeze feels like blessing.
The robin’s call, a reminder.
Each leaf that turns
is him, giving again.

And I, still learning how to let go,
am also learning how to say
thank you.

title: Poem - With Soft Eyes
html:
I walked to the field where the grasses lean,
where the earth breathes slow beneath bare feet,
and the wind—never in a hurry—
waited for me to stop hurrying too.

I laid down what I was carrying:
the clenched fists of thought,
the forward-straining heart,
the eyes that search for something not yet here.

A small pause opened in the spine of the world,
like a sigh in the ribs of a deer,
or the hush that settles
just before a robin sings.

There—
in that barely-there stillness,
the kind that moss knows,
and minnows, and dusk on still water—
I remembered how to arrive.

No grand entrance.
No need to deserve the moment.
Just the soft fact of it.
Just breath and the tender weight of being.

The birch did not ask what I’d achieved.
The stone did not require a reason.
The world, unshaken by my unrest,
offered me a place anyway.

So I knelt.
Pressed the pads of my fingers into the soil.
Let the ground say what it always says:
You are held. You are here. You are already enough.

And when I rose,
the eyes I opened were not the same—
softer now, like rain arriving without sound,
like dawn remembering its own name.

I saw myself then—
not as a task,
but as part of the living world—
and the world, seeing me,
did not turn away.

title: Poem - The Softest Thing
html:
It was not thunder that opened me—
not fire, not wind tearing the leaves—
but something quieter.
A mossy unfolding,
a small bird landing on the ribcage
with no need to explain itself.

I had thought the heart a gate
guarded by iron and memory.
But it was only
a wet petal,
waiting to be noticed,
waiting to be touched
with the back of my own hand.

The angry voice,
so long mistaken for truth,
sank back like frost
when the sun comes carefully
over the edge of the field.

And then I heard it—
not a word,
but the feeling of being forgiven
by the forest,
by the river,
by myself.

So I stayed there,
breathing with the birch trees,
smiling at the stone
who never once asked me to be better—
only to stay awhile
and be real, to be me.

title: Poem - The widening field
html:
At first, the body is small—
a sparrow tucking its wings,
hushed against the weight of the sky.
The heart folds itself inward,
a secret stone in the pocket of the earth.

But then—
a breath, a loosening,
the river unfreezing in its bed.
A hand rests gently on the chest,
and already the world
leans closer in kindness.

Roots grow unseen,
the spine remembers the tree,
the ground carries you as if you were
always meant to be carried.

And slowly, the voice inside
learns to hum like a meadow at dawn,
the hands press outward,
not in defence,
but as branches meeting air.

At last the gaze widens—
horizon pouring in through the eyes,
arms opening like wings,
as if the sky itself
had been waiting for you to arrive.

This is how it happens—
a softening, a receiving, a rooting,
until you discover you are
not a fragment
but a whole field of belonging,
wide enough
for all the weather of your heart.

title: Poem - The others were already there
html:
I had walked for years
believing it was mine to carry —
the sorrow, the tension,
the tangle of stories
no one had time to hear.

I thought that was strength:
to hold it alone,
to speak only when neat,
to keep the trembling parts
tucked quietly beneath the doing.

But the truth is —
the redwoods do not stand
in solitude.

Their roots intertwine
beneath the forest floor,
hidden,
but holding.

A shared net of nourishment.
A silent web of weathering.
Not one tree survives a storm alone.

And somewhere,
in a field where the wind had room
to pass unhurried,
I met a small circle
of humans —
tired,
quiet,
real.

No one said much at first.
No one asked for my history.

They just sat —
the way a fire sits,
patient and warm.

And in that gentle company,
my nervous system —
so used to bracing —
let go.

Not because I was fixed.
Not because I was ready.
But because
I was not alone.

Because someone else’s breath
rose and fell beside mine.
Because someone else’s silence
did not demand explanation.
Because someone else’s presence
felt like a soft hand on the back,
wordless,
but steady.

That evening,
I lay beneath the trembling stars,
no longer trying to make meaning.
The meaning was in the togetherness.
In the simple, holy act
of sitting near someone
who dared to soften too.

And when I left,
I did not leave empty.

I carried the trace
of something older than independence —
something forest-wide,
something ancestral —
the deep remembering
that healing
was never meant
to be done
alone.

title: Poem - The moment I said yes
html:
It didn’t look like much —
just a path curving into dune grass,
a pale sky opening its palms
to the sea.

I wasn’t seeking transformation.
I wasn’t lost, exactly.
Just… tired.

Of the pace.
Of the shoulds.
Of the clever ways I avoided myself
in the name of being “fine.”

And yet,
something —
soft but certain —
said,
Come this way.

So I did.

I walked not in search of answers
but to remember
how it feels
to walk without bracing.

And the world —
wild and unconcerned —
welcomed me.

The wind asked nothing of me.
The light didn’t care
what I had achieved.
Even the sand —
messy, shifting,
utterly itself —
seemed to say,
This too is allowed.

I sat on a stone
older than my sorrow.
I breathed.
No great epiphany came.

But something small —
and real —
began to reassemble.

Not a new life.
But a new way
of meeting the one I already had.

Slower.
Softer.
With more room
for what I had long silenced.

Later,
I would return
to the same walls,
the same inbox,
the same rhythm.

But I
would not be the same.

And in some unknowable tomorrow,
my future self —
wiser,
steadier,
a little more free —
would look back on this one quiet turning
and whisper,
Thank you.

Not for doing it all.
Not for getting it perfect.

But for saying yes.
Yes to the breath.
Yes to the pause.
Yes to the life
waiting
beneath
the noise.

title: Poem - The first warmth returns
html:
There was a long season when nothing inside me moved.
Not toward others, not toward myself.
Even the small gestures —
the ones that once came naturally — fell silent,
like birds forgetting their own migration routes.

I thought something essential had vanished,
the way a river disappears underground
and no one knows if it will rise again.

But one ordinary morning,
as the light touched the edge of the kitchen table,
I felt a shift — a tenderness so faint
it might have been imagined.
A filament of warmth threaded through my chest,
asking nothing, promising nothing,
simply reminding me that care had not died, only rested.

I placed a hand there, lightly,
as if greeting a long-lost friend I did not want to startle.
And the breath met my hand with a softness I had not felt in years.

It was enough. Enough to know
that contribution does not return
as a task
or a role
or a duty.
It returns as a quiet willingness — the body leaning
one millimetre toward life again.

I stood by the window, watching the early light
brush the fields with its patient touch,
and something in me whispered:
I am still capable of warmth.
I am still threaded to this world.
I can begin again from here.

title: Poem - This moment is enough
html:
You don’t need to settle.
You don’t need to focus.
You don’t need to get anywhere.

Just notice…
you are already here.

If your eyes want to move,
that’s fine.
If your body wants to shift,
let it.

Attention can come and go.
Nothing needs holding.

If the mind jumps,
that’s okay.
If it pauses,
that’s okay too.

There is no task hidden here.
Nothing you’re meant to do.

Just notice
where your body is supported.

The chair.
The floor.
The ground beneath you.

You don’t have to press down.
Just let yourself be held
for this moment.

Breath can be however it is.

Fast.
Slow.
Uneven.
Or barely noticed at all.

Even when it wanders,
it belongs.

If a sound pulls your attention,
let it.
If a sensation pulls you,
that’s fine too.

You are not doing this wrong.

Just notice one small thing
that feels neutral…
or okay.

A temperature.
A colour.
A point of contact.

You don’t need to stay with it.

Noticing once
is enough.

Your system is allowed to move
and rest
at the same time.

There is nothing to fix.
Nothing to finish.
Nothing you are falling behind on
right now.

Even with movement.
Even with noise inside.

You are still here.

And that is enough
for this moment.

title: Poem - What comes back on its own
html:
I did not chase it.
I did not call its name into the dark.

I sat where the ground could feel me
and let the morning do what mornings do
when no one interferes.

Some things return
only when they are no longer summoned.

The creek does not rush itself.
The fox does not announce hunger.
Seeds open in their own weather.

I had mistaken silence for absence,
stillness for failure.
But the body remembers things
the mind was never meant to manage.

There was a time
when wanting became dangerous,
when the door closed quietly
so nothing else would be lost.

So I learned the art of not asking.
Of living in the hallway.
Of touching the world lightly
so it wouldn’t notice me.

But the earth never forgot my shape.

One afternoon
the warmth arrived without instruction,
low in the body,
like sunlight finding the floor
after years of dust.

Nothing dramatic.
No music.
Just a soft yes
that did not need explanation.

This is how life returns—
not as fire,
but as permission.

Not as urgency,
but as breath.

I am not late.
I am not broken.
I am right on time
for what grows slowly
and stays.

title: Poem - Stillness, found
html:
It wasn’t something you entered.
It was already there,
beneath the reaching
and the stepping back.

The body paused
not because it was told to,
but because nothing was pulling hard enough
to tear it in two.

Warmth stayed where it belonged.
Edges softened without opening.
Breath moved like weather
passing through a field
that didn’t need to change.

There was no leaning toward.
No retreat.
Just the quiet fact of being here
inside your own outline.

Stillness didn’t arrive as silence.
It came as permission
to stop negotiating with the moment.

And for a while,
that was enough.

title: Poem - Where the river widens
html:
The river didn’t stop
because it was tired of moving.

It widened.

What once rushed between narrow banks
began to slow
not from resistance
but from having room.

Birdsong still crossed the water.
Light still moved.
Nothing precious was lost.

The current learned
it didn’t have to prove
it was alive.

Upstream, the hills kept offering themselves.
Downstream, the sea waited
without urgency.

No one asked the river
what it meant.
No one needed it to arrive anywhere.

It carried what it carried.
It rested where it could.

And in that widening,
something settled —
not silence,
not stillness,
but a deeper permission
to be exactly as full
as it already was.

title: Poem - What waits beneath winter
html:
Nothing was wrong with the field
because it did not bloom.

The ground held its colour inward.
Seeds stayed folded,
not asleep,
not awake —
just waiting.

Frost came and went.
Tracks crossed the surface
and faded again.

Below, something listened.

No one asked the earth
to explain itself.
No one hurried the light.

Roots stayed busy
in ways the sky could not see.
Time moved slowly enough
to be trusted.

And when warmth returned,
it did not arrive as instruction.
It came as a suggestion —
a loosening,
a soft yes
the soil recognised
without effort.

Nothing had been missing.
Only resting
in the dark
until the season changed.

title: Poem - Between tide and shore
html:
Some days the sea came close,
lifting shells,
rewriting the edge of the land
as if it had plans.

Other days it pulled back,
leaving long stretches of sand
exposed, unsure
what they were for.

Nothing was broken in the coming.
Nothing was lost in the leaving.

The moon kept its distance,
faithful without instruction.
The shore learned the rhythm
by staying.

Water touched.
Water withdrew.
Each time, the ground remained.

No one asked the tide
to choose a side.
No one told the shore
to follow.

And slowly,
without decision,
a steadier knowing formed —
that movement could happen
without carrying everything away,
and stillness could arrive
without meaning disappearing.

What stayed was not the wave
and not the sand,
but the place where they met
again
and again
without explanation.

title: Poem - What stays when the light shifts
html:
Some days the valley filled with birds.
Wingbeats everywhere,
air alive with direction.

Other days the same land
lay quiet,
as if nothing had ever passed through.

The mountains did not argue with the weather.
They did not rush the sun back into place
or apologise for the shade.

Snow came.
Melt followed.
Rivers rose, then thinned again
without forgetting their course.

No one asked the ground
to explain its timing.
No one told the trees
to decide once and for all
whether it was spring.

Roots kept working
in the dark intervals.
Stone held its patience.

And slowly it became clear:
nothing essential was leaving
when the brightness dimmed,
and nothing dangerous arrived
when it returned.

What endured was not the season,
not the colour,
not the song —

but the land itself,
wide enough to hold
arrival and absence
without having to choose.

title: Poem - While the light is here
html:
The evening did not hurry when it began to thin.

Light loosened its hold on the tops of trees,
slid quietly along the river,
rested for a moment on the backs of stones.

Nothing in the field seemed surprised.
The grass did not cling to the sun.
The birds did not petition for one more hour.

They moved as if the leaving had always been part of the song.

Somewhere, a gate closed softly.
Somewhere else, a window opened to the cooling air.
Breath entered. Breath left.
The sky held both.

There was no announcement that this colour of gold
would not return in quite the same way.
No warning that this particular arrangement of cloud and shadow
would never gather again.

And still, the world did not tremble.
It widened.
Hands that had been busy became still.
Faces turned toward what remained without trying to preserve it.

And for a moment — small, unrepeatable —
everything that was alive was simply alive.
Not proving.
Not securing.
Not postponing.

Just here.

The light thinned further.
Dark gathered without cruelty.

Somewhere, a child laughed.
Somewhere, someone closed their eyes.

The sky did not choose between them.
It held both as it has always done.

And in that holding there was no urgency —
only the quiet astonishment that this breath has come at all.

While it is here.

title: Poem - The slow turning
html:
The days moved
without announcing themselves.

Light crossed the floor,
shifted from one wall to another,
and no one marked the distance.

Leaves changed colour
one by one,
not as a signal
but as a quiet agreement
with the season.

The river did not rush
to prove it was moving.
It curved,
and curved again,
as it always had.

Somewhere beneath the soil
roots kept their patient count —
not of hours,
but of growth.

Nothing dramatic was required.

The sky widened each evening
whether or not anyone looked up.

And in that widening
there was no demand —
only the simple fact
that this moment, too,
belongs
to a longer turning.

title: Poem - The edge and the horizon
html:
There are days
when the horizon comes close.

You can feel it in the ribs —
that thin, bright line
where sky meets earth
and nothing lasts.

The air sharpens.
Colours deepen.
Every sound carries weight.

You stand still
as if the ground itself
has spoken.

Then the world resumes.

Kettles boil.
Phones ring.
Dust gathers in the corners
as it always has.

The horizon steps back
without apology.

You forget the sharpness
for a while.

Or think you do.

But sometimes, in the middle of a task,
a door closes somewhere
and the echo travels further
than it should.

A leaf falls
without drama.
A shadow lengthens
before you notice.

The body remembers
what the mind cannot hold.

It remembers the edge.

And yet —
the river continues.

Not in defiance.
Not in denial.

It curves through stone
that has outlived forests.
It moves under stars
that burn without urgency.

Nothing hurries it.

Not the mountain.
Not the sea.

The edge is always there.
And so is the horizon.

They do not fight.

They widen each other.

And somewhere between them
— between the knowing
and the forgetting —
breath enters
and leaves
without explanation.

The sky does not demand
that you choose.

It holds the vastness
and the smallness
together.

While the light shifts.

title: Poem - Between the star and the stone
html:
Some nights the sky comes closer.
You feel it in the ribs — that widening —
as if the dark itself is breathing with you.

Stars sharpen. Distances stretch beyond measure.
For a moment, everything small rearranges.
The hand on the table.
The sound of someone moving in another room.

The simple fact of being here.
It all feels improbable. Precious. Unrepeatable.
Then morning returns. Kettles boil. Emails arrive.
Shoes by the door wait to be worn.

The sky lifts itself higher, as if it had never leaned in.
And still, somewhere beneath the day, the widening remains.

The stone in the field does not argue with the stars.
It holds their light when it falls and holds its own weight when it doesn’t.

The river moves whether anyone stands at its edge counting the years.
It carries fallen leaves and bright reflections alike without deciding which matters more.

Clouds gather. Clouds dissolve. Mountains remain without clinging to the shape of weather.
Nothing here rushes to justify itself.
Nothing postpones its own ending.

The tide arrives and withdraws without regret.
And between the star and the stone,
between the widening and the returning,
breath enters and leaves without needing to choose.

The sky does not demand that you hold it open.
The earth does not ask that you forget it.
They widen each other.

And somewhere in that widening — quiet, unannounced —
life continues without urgency, without denial,

simply held in something vast enough to include both the edge and the ordinary.

title: Poem - Still, the Warmth
html:
The world does not pause for our comfort.
Wind moves across oceans without asking who feels ready for it.

Cities wake to headlines, roads fill with motion,
voices rise and fall in places we will never see.

Somewhere, storms gather.
Somewhere, something breaks.
Somewhere, something begins again.

And yet— the morning still opens.
Light arrives through the quiet gap between two clouds.

A bird crosses the sky without carrying the weight of the whole horizon.
Grass bends to the same wind that moves the distant sea.

The earth does not wait for certainty.
It simply holds.

Stone beneath soil. Roots beneath stone.
Water moving slowly through unseen ground.

And here— in the small shelter of the body—
breath enters as it always has.
Ribs widen.
Air leaves again without needing permission from the future.

Warmth gathers where the hands rest.
A quiet place no storm can fully reach.

The world may remain wide, unsettled, turning through its endless changes.
Clouds will travel. Rivers will rise and fall.
The wind will carry both cold and fragrance.

But inside this brief morning moment something softer remains.
A warmth not borrowed from certainty.
A steadiness not dependent on tomorrow.

Just this— breath moving through the chest,
ground beneath the feet, and the quiet knowing
that even in a restless world a small human heart can still open
like a field receiving the sun.

title: Poem - While the world turns
html:
The world does not grow quiet
for our comfort.

Wind moves across oceans.
Clouds gather and dissolve.
Somewhere a storm begins
while somewhere else
morning light touches a field.

The earth holds all of it
without choosing sides.

And here,
inside the shelter of the ribs,
breath continues.

It arrives
without waiting for certainty.

It leaves
without asking what comes next.

A tree stands in the wind
because its roots are deep.

And something like that
is possible here too—

a small warmth
in the middle of a changing world,

breath rising,
breath falling,

while the world
continues to turn.

title: Poem - Enough, before the day begins
html:
The day does not arrive all at once.

It gathers. In small sounds.
In light touching the edges of things.
In the quiet way the body wakes
before the mind begins its counting.

There is already movement in the world.
Cars passing somewhere unseen.
Voices beginning.
Weather shifting across distances
that do not ask for your permission.

And still— here— something has not rushed.
Breath enters without needing a plan.
Leaves again without needing certainty.
The floor has not moved away.
The chair has not withdrawn its support.

The small, unnoticed agreements of the world are still holding.
Gravity remains faithful.
The body remembers how to be carried.

And even if the mind is already reaching ahead—
toward tasks, toward people, toward things not yet shaped— something quieter stays behind.
Not stuck. Just here.

A hand resting on the chest finds warmth without asking if it is deserved.
Feet meet the ground without checking if they are ready.
Nothing announces this.
Nothing declares it important.
But it is happening.

A quiet sufficiency before the day begins asking.
Not everything solved.
Not everything steady.
But something— enough.

Enough to sit.
Enough to breathe.
Enough to take one step
when the moment comes.

And perhaps that is all the morning ever needed to offer.
Not certainty. Not control.
Just this:
a body already held,
a breath already moving,
and a beginning that does not require more than what is already here.

title: Poem - Still, something remains
html:
The sky does not wait
for everything to settle.

Cloud moves through cloud.
Light shifts
without asking
what came before.

Wind crosses the field
on every kind of day.

Grass bends
whether it is easy
or not.

A river continues
through clear water
and rough.

Stone remains beneath it.

And here—

breath enters
without waiting
for things to improve.

Leaves again
without needing to know
what comes next.

Feet meet the ground
that has not moved.

Hands rest
without asking if they are ready.

Not everything settles.

Not everything becomes clear.

And still—

something remains.

Nothing has to be resolved
for this to be here.

Just this—

breath moving,
ground beneath,
and something quiet
that has not left.

title: Poem - A little space opens
html:
The sky does not ask the weather to settle before it becomes wide. Cloud passes through cloud, and still there is space. Light finds its way between what does not part, touching the edges of things without needing them to change.

A field does not wait for the wind to soften. It receives what arrives, and lets it move on. Grass bends and rises again, not deciding when it is ready, not holding on to what has already passed through.

A river continues, whether the surface is smooth or unsettled. Water moves over stone, around it, carrying what it can. Beneath the shifting surface, something steady remains, unseen but unchanged.

And here— in the quiet shape of the body— something similar. Breath entering without asking how this moment is. Leaving again without needing it to become easier. The ground has not shifted. The body is still here.

And in a place so small it could be missed, a little space opens. Not made. Not held. Just there. Enough for this moment to be met, exactly as it is.

title: Poem - The Gardener Knows
html:
The gardener does not argue with the soil.
She kneels beside it and asks
what it needs.

The hard ground is not broken ground.
It is ground that has been holding on,
doing its job
without anyone noticing.

She does not force it open.
She returns, and returns again —
water, air, the quiet turning of a hand —
until one morning the earth
gives way a little.

Not because it surrendered.
Because it was tended.

Joy does not arrive on command.
It comes the way a seed comes —
when the ground has been made ready,
when there is space
for a root to find its way.

The gardener knows this.
She does not watch for the shoot.
She tends the soil,
and trusts the season.

And in the waiting, she notices:
her hands are already warm.
The ground beneath them
already beginning
to remember
what it is for.

title: Poem - The Hand on the Heart
html:
There is a weight this morning
that is not grief, exactly —
more like the afterweight of weather,
the sky after the storm has passed
but hasn't said so yet.

The mind knows what it knows.
It has already sorted the night,
filed the words that were not meant for you,
returned the verdict: not guilty,
not the cause, not the cure.

But the body keeps its own records.
Writes in a different alphabet —
weight, and held breath, and the slight
contraction around what was said.
The body is not slow. It is precise.
It is keeping something safe
until it is sure there is somewhere to put it.

So offer it this:
the slow stroke of a hand on the forearm,
patient as water, warm as intention,
moving at the speed care actually moves —
slower than you think, more real than you expect.

And then this:
both hands on the chest.
Still. Present. Not fixing.
Just the oldest conversation:
a body asking its own body
if it is alright.

Now ask:
if this hand could speak —
if it were the friend who has always known you,
the one who was there before the words,
before the story, before the night —
what would it say?

Listen.

It says: I love you.

Not because you handled it well.
Not because you kept it together
or were patient enough
or said the right thing.
Not because of anything.

Just: I love you.

The way the body always has —
quietly, without condition,
through every morning you thought
you would not move through,
and then did.

Stay here a moment.
Let the words go somewhere real.
Not into thinking — lower,
into the place the weight was.

Now notice:
is it the same as when you began?
It is enough that something moved.
It is enough that you asked.
It is enough that the hand knew
what to say.

title: Poem - What the Seed Knows
html:
The seed does not decide to germinate.
It responds to conditions —
moisture, warmth, the particular darkness
of soil that has been turned.

It has been alive all winter.
Not visibly. Not dramatically.
But the small chemistry of it
has been running without pause,
holding everything ready
for exactly this.

We do not see germination begin.
We see it only after it has already been
happening for some time —
the first pale thread of root
already several days old
when it finally becomes visible.

This is how aliveness works.
Not arriving. Already present.
Already moving through its quiet stages
below the surface we can see.

The gardener’s second work
is not to make things grow.
It is to recognise
that growing is already happening —
to learn the art of noticing
what was never not alive.

title: Poem - What the Soil Holds
html:
Press a hand to the earth in April
and feel it.
Not cold, not warm in any dramatic sense —
just the specific temperature
of ground that has been holding
the sun’s heat from the day before.

It does not announce this.
It simply holds it,
the way a body holds its own warmth
through the night —
quietly, without effort,
as a matter of course.

The gardener kneels and brings one hand
to the inside of the wrist.
She is not checking for something wrong.
She is noticing what is already running —
the small, continuous heat
of a body doing its work.

This is what she came to find:
not warmth she would need to bring,
but warmth she could finally
stop walking past.

The soil was never cold.
It was waiting for someone
to kneel close enough
to feel it

title: Poem - What the Shoot Does Not Know
html:
It does not decide to reach.
It simply responds to the direction
from which the light arrives.

Press both feet into the floor for a moment.
Feel the floor push back.
This is what the shoot is doing —
finding out what is solid,
learning the direction of up.

It is not trying to become anything.
It is not performing growth.
It is doing the only thing available:
responding to what is actually here,
one millimetre at a time,
without a plan.

A brow released.
A wrist that circles for no reason.
The corners of a mouth
inclining, slightly, toward something
it has not yet named.

This is sufficient.
This is, in fact, exactly what
the whole season
has been preparing for:

not the arrival of joy,
but the quiet, unhurried moment
when the body remembers
that reaching toward the light
was always something it knew how to do.

title: Poem - The Gardener Rests
html:
She does not stand at the edge of the garden
watching for what she has planted.
She has learned that watching
is not the same as tending,
and tending is not the same as growing,
and growing is not something
she has ever been able to do.

She rests one hand against her own face.
Feels the warmth of the palm,
the warmth of the cheek,
the meeting of the two.

Five mornings she came here.
Five times she knelt in the cold
and did the only things available:
turned what was compacted,
noticed what was already alive,
offered warmth to what had been waiting,
made a little room for something
she could not yet name.

She does not know what will come.
She knows what she has done.
She knows the difference between those two things,
and she has made her peace with it.

The spine finds its length without effort.
The breath moves in and takes its time leaving.
The soil is warm.

This is what the season asked of her.
She gave it.
Now she rests.
